source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "វិធីបណ្តុះកូនល្ហុង" (Method for Raising Papaya Seedlings), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
While seedlings are in the nursery, keep them under shade netting and water them regularly so the soil in the bags stays moist but not waterlogged. Watch for damping-off or wilting, which signals the soil is too wet or the seedlings are overcrowded.

Seedlings are generally ready to move to the field after about 25–30 days in the nursery bag, once they have a sturdy stem and healthy leaves. If seedlings start to grow tall and thin (spindly) before this window, farmers should transplant them a little earlier rather than let them become leggy and weak.

When transplanting, choose a cloudy day or the cooler part of the late afternoon/evening to reduce transplant shock, and check that the root ball has not become root-bound inside the bag before planting it out.
